premises: Pore architecture (size distribution, porosity) can be systematically controlled in rare-earth zirconate HECs via TBA gel-casting with varying solid loadings.
The controlled micron-scale pores act as additional phonon scattering centers that reduce phonon mean free path and thermal conductivity.
A CALPHAD-guided predictive framework can be extended to incorporate pore architecture descriptors.
Integrating pore descriptors with CALPHAD will improve prediction accuracy of low thermal conductivity by ~15% over CALPHAD-only methods.
The specific composition (La0.25Eu0.25Gd0.25Yb0.25)2(Zr0.75Ce0.25)2O7 can achieve room-temperature thermal conductivity below 0.07 W/(m·K) with the targeted pore architecture.
